    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I and deal 1 face down on top.     {"id":"Q03","answer":"Yes, you may take a Reveal turn with Agents left; after Revealing, you are skipped for the rest of Player Turns and cannot take a later Agent turn that round.     {"id":"Q04","answer":"A Plot Intrigue played during your own Agent turn may grant resources before placement, and those resources may pay that visit’s entry cost.     {"id":"Q05","answer":"Deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus at most 2 of the 4 troops already in your garrison, for up to 5. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not allowed. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison before deployment.","support":"supported","evidence":"Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison, at a Combat space; cube recruits from supply into garrison."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"A Spy Agent icon on the played card allows the Agent to go to any space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; that Spy stays there. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent on that destination; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card when you send an Agent, chosen immediately after placing the Agent and before any space/card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both; on one placement you may use different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather Intelligence timing and distinct Spy restrictions."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"Strength is 2×2 troop + 1×3 sandworm + 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot play Combat Intrigue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Strength: troops 2 each, sandworms 3, swords 1; last unit removed means 0. Intrigue cards: Combat only if at least one unit deployed."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again if an opponent plays; the Combat Intrigue window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player’s supply, Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to the bank.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: players may play or pass; not required to pass after earlier pass; consecutive passes close. Cleanup returns troops, resets markers, returns worms."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"With exactly two tied for first in a four-player Conflict, each tied player gets the second reward; the other two compete for the third reward. No one wins the Conflict and nobody takes its card. In a three-player Conflict, the two tied first each get second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat ties: exactly two tied first with 4 players leaves others competing for third; 3 or fewer give no other rewards. Strength/rewards: zero strength no reward."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; multiple worms do not multiply it again. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice once for 1 VP, or pay 6 spice to take it twice for 2 VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons cannot; optional cost may be paid again (3 spice example)."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it against your other face-up Conflict or Objective cards. Matching is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icon types in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Battle Icons: winner takes card, check matching face-up Conflict or Objective; must flip pair; Endgame wild match."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; you lose that VP below 2 and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gains the Alliance token and 1 VP; that VP follows token possession. Tying the holder does not steal it: a challenger must rise above the holder. If the holder loses Influence while previously tied, FAQ transfer rules apply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 VP reversal; 4 track bonus retained; Alliance token temporary VP; tying does not transfer."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"During your Reveal turn, Persuasion can be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one purchase and split one source across several purchases. The Imperium Row is replenished to five, so you may buy the replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.","support":"supported","evidence":"Acquiring Cards: Reveal timing, pool/split, replace missing Row cards, acquired card enters discard."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"At Makers, put 1 spice in each Maker space with no Agent, adding to existing bonus spice; a visitor gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Sandworms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while Shield Wall remains; removing it permits worms at any Conflict. Hooks are only required where the effect specifies them, and are retained rather than spent. A worm goes directly to your Conflict, never your garrison.","support":"supported","evidence":"Makers; Sandworms; Board Space Guide entries for Deep Desert and Hagga Basin."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"At Recall, after the round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. First, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues; then compare VP. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then troops in garrison.","support":"supported","evidence":"Recall phase and Scoring: endgame trigger at end of a round; Endgame Intrigue before winner; ordered tiebreakers."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Standard CHOAM setup exposes 2 face-up contract offers and puts the remaining 18 standard tokens face down in the bank. Shuffle 4 additional Intrigue cards into that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of standard setup.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM setup changes: 20 contracts shuffled, two offers, 18 bank; add 4 cards each; Shaddam optional. Contrasting-back set excluded."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"With CHOAM and available contracts, the icon lets you take one face-up contract and replace it with a face-up token from the bank; without CHOAM, or when all contracts have been taken by players, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes when an Agent visits a Maker space and the player gains the stated total spice that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.","support":"supported","evidence":"Human contract icon table; Completing contracts definitions."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait for a future turn because you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, take its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Completing contracts: must hold at time of Agent placement; completion procedure."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose card shows First Player takes that marker. First Player alternates only between humans; turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival takes Agent turns only and never Reveals.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, and immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects; apply only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rival Agent turns: skip occupied destinations; Place Spy handling; ignore normal costs/effects; reshuffle."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"For 3–4 players, shuffle the eligible Objectives after removing cards with a mismatched 1–3P or 4/6P mark, then deal one face up to each player. The card showing the First Player marker determines the first player. Shaddam may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; match player-count marking, shuffle, distribute face up, marked card sets First Player."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"The bank’s Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make any convenient substitution if they run out. Troops are limited by a player’s supply: if it is empty, that player cannot recruit more until troops return. Payments of Solari, spice or water return to the bank.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup step 7: bank resources not meant to be limited; gains from bank and payments returned; troop recruitment rule."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict from the top and place it face up beside the deck, on top of any unclaimed prior Conflict cards; then each player draws five cards. If Endgame does not trigger at Recall, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, while in 2P return Rival Agents to supply and pass the marker to the other human, then start next round.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure phases; Round Start reveal before drawing; Recall next-round preparation."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Yes, you may resolve the board-space effects, played card’s Agent-box effects, and Faction Influence advance in any order. No, you must pay entry costs and meet requirements before resolving those effects, so that visit’s Influence cannot meet its own entry requirement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Agent Turn: entry cost/requirements first; then effects and Influence in any order."},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"No. An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid only once per turn; you are not forced to pay and get no effect if you decline. Most card and space effects are mandatory, except “may,” optional arrow costs and optional black-X trash; direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Arrows / paying costs; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs."},
    {"id":"Q26","answer":"The Spy icon places a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post; some effects require the post be connected to a specified Agent icon, and then you cannot use another type. If you have no Spy in supply, you may first recall one of your own deployed Spies for no effect, then place it.","support":"supported","evidence":"Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post, recall one if supply empty; specified Agent-icon connection constraint."},
    {"id":"Q27","answer":"No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, not your own. Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence recall is available without a card, but an Agent-turn card is still required to send an Agent. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you can recall one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.","support":"supported","evidence":"Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says card still required; may recall two for distinct effects, never two Gather Intelligence."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"When anyone visits a controlled Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, the controller gains 1 Solari; for Imperial Basin, the controller gains 1 spice. The visitor also receives the space’s own effects, including if visitor is controller. A critical-location Conflict winner replaces the prior Control marker with theirs. When a Conflict is revealed for a space already controlled, its controller may deploy 1 troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without visiting.","support":"supported","evidence":"Critical Locations & Control; Board Space Guide says resolve visitor and controller effects separately."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"For a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their first reward and card, and no further rewards are given. A tie for third receives nothing. Three tied for first each get the second reward, nobody takes the card, and nobody gets other rewards, in either three- or four-player play.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat ties and three tied for first table."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"In a three-player Conflict with three distinct positive strengths, first and second receive their printed rewards; third receives nothing. This is the same in a two-human game with the Rival participating: 2P is treated as a three-player game for ranks, so only ordinary first and second are paid.","support":"supported","evidence":"Resolve Combat: with 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second get rewards; ordinary third none; Rival counts in 2P."},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Plot Intrigues are playable during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and with at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separate from your deck, and after resolving one put it face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue Deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.","support":"supported","evidence":"Intrigue cards timing and storage; FAQ Draw timing says reshuffle Intrigue discard when deck runs out."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"No, an ordinary discard instruction means a card of your choice from your hand and not an Intrigue unless specified. The Steal Intrigue icon makes each opponent who has 4 or more Intrigues give you one selected at random.","support":"supported","evidence":"Discarding; Intrigue cards—Steal Intrigue icon."},

    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down on the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: face-down 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused cards without looking."},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"Both setups start with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in the player's garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water. The score marker starts at 1 in a four-player game and 0 in a three-player game.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, Swordmaster beside board, three troops garrisoned, nine in supply, 1 water."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing you skip the rest of Player Turns and cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. On Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.","support":"supported","evidence":"Player Turns: Agent turns optional; once Revealed, turns are skipped. Reveal: resolve just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard."},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"A Plot Intrigue may be played before placing your Agent, and resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may be revealed instead.","support":"supported","evidence":"Player Turns: Plot can be played first, and its pre-placement grants can pay entry; later gains cannot. Agent Turn: choose one icon; no-icon cards only on Reveal."},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during this turn may deploy, plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for at most five deployed from those sources. At a non-Combat space, normal deployment is not allowed. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.","support":"supported","evidence":"Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison, only at a Combat space; cube recruits a troop from supply into garrison."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"The Spy Agent icon on a card lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; the Spy stays there. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at that destination, but not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent and before receiving space or card effects to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both, though two different Spies can be used for the two effects. A Spy cannot be recalled for both effects on the same placement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence recall connected Spies; Gather is chosen just after placement before effects."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"Strength is 2 troops × 2 + 1 sandworm × 3 + 4 swords = 11. If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. You cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window without at least one unit in the Conflict.","support":"supported","evidence":"Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; at least one Conflict unit is required. Combat Intrigue: eligible players have at least one unit."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Yes. Passing earlier does not bar you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and all Combat markers reset to 0.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat: a player need not pass just because they passed earlier; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply, resets markers, and returns sandworms to bank."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"With exactly two tied for first in four-player play, each tied player gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward. Nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. With two tied for first in a three-player game, each gets the second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat ties: first-place tie gives second reward; in four players exactly two tied first leave other players competing for third; no tied-first winner/card. Zero strength gets no reward."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Having one or more sandworms doubles the rewards once; additional worms do not multiply it further. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay 3 spice a second time to take that reward again, for 2 VP total at 6 spice; paying only once yields one instance.","support":"supported","evidence":"Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double rewards; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward costs may be paid a second time."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"After winning a Conflict, take its card face up into your supply, then check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP; it is not optional. At Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three battle icons in your supply, and the pair is flipped for 1 VP.","support":"supported","evidence":"Combat winner procedure and Battle Icons: take card, then mandatory match check; eligible face-up cards and Endgame wild match."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, and regain it on returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning; the first to 4 also takes the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which is lost if the token leaves. Merely tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not take the token; you must rise above them. The FAQ separately says that if the holder loses Influence after a tie, the formerly tied player takes it (or, if several were tied, the former holder chooses). If the holder falls to 3 or lower and no one has 4+, it returns to the board.","support":"supported","evidence":"Victory Points—Faction Influence: separate 2- and 4-Influence rewards and Alliance transfer rules; FAQ Alliance loss clarification."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"During Reveal, spend Persuasion to acquire Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. The cost is at the card's top right. You may pool Persuasion sources to buy one card or split a source across purchases, and acquire cards before, between, or after Reveal effects. The Row refills to five immediately, so you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile; unused Persuasion is lost.","support":"supported","evidence":"Acquiring Cards: Reveal purchases, top-right cost, pooling/splitting, Row replacement, discard destination, and unused Persuasion lost."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"At Makers, each Agent-free Maker space gains one spice in its bonus spot, adding to any already there; visiting a Maker space collects all accumulated bonus spice. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Hooks are not spent when summoning. A sandworm cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; after its removal it may be summoned to any Conflict, but never placed in a garrison.","support":"supported","evidence":"Makers; Deep Desert/Hagga Basin space guide; Sandworms: Hooks requirement/retention and Shield Wall restrictions."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"At the end of a round, reaching 10 or more VP or emptying the Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. The listed resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scoring / Victory Conditions: game end, Endgame Intrigues, winner and tiebreakers."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"Standard CHOAM starts with 20 standard contracts shuffled face down; two are exposed as face-up offers and the remaining 18 stay face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into the Intrigue Deck and four additional Imperium cards into the Imperium Deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left out of standard CHOAM.","support":"supported","evidence":"CHOAM setup changes and Components: two offers from 20; four added cards in each deck; contrasting-back contracts only for Rise of Ix."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"With CHOAM and available contracts, take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a bank contract flipped face up. If players have taken all contracts, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract requires visiting a Maker space and gaining its stated spice total that turn, including other sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.","support":"supported","evidence":"Taking contracts and Completing contracts; shared contract-icon rule."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"No. You must have held a board-space contract when you sent the Agent there, so one taken after visiting must wait until a future visit. When completed, announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Completing contracts: must hold it when sending Agent; on completion announce, gain rewards, flip face down, keep in supply."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to the humans. First Player is whichever human's Objective shows the marker, and First Player alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type; if none exists, ignore placement, then immediately reveal another card. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.","support":"supported","evidence":"Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle rule."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"Shuffle the Objective cards after omitting those marked for a different player count, then deal one eligible Objective face up to each player; its First Player marker selects the first player. Shaddam Corrino IV may be chosen only when using the CHOAM Module.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: omit player-count mismatches, shuffle, deal face up; Shaddam not used unless playing CHOAM."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if they run out. By contrast, you cannot recruit more troops if your personal supply is empty until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments are returned to it; the summary does not say to take resources from another player's supply.","support":"supported","evidence":"Setup: resources and sandworms are not meant to be limited; gains from bank and payments return to bank. Recruiting: empty troop supply prevents recruiting."},
